compose-capture-env.authority: env: whole process environment (HOME, PATH, AHO_*, credential variables)
compose-capture-env.reason: Inputs::from_process is documented as the only place that reads the process environment, snapshotting vars_os into Inputs.env once so composition downstream works from captured, testable inputs and fails with NoHome when HOME is empty.

compose-read-config.authority: fs: read one aho config layer file
compose-read-config.reason: read_optional reads exactly the layer path the composer hands it and turns NotFound into None, so an absent aho.toml or ~/.aho/config.toml is an empty layer rather than an error.

compose-write-config.authority: fs: atomic write of an aho config layer file
compose-write-config.reason: write_atomic creates the parent directory, writes `<path>.tmp` and renames it over the target so `aho apply`/`aho set` never leave a half-written layer file for readers.

compose-probe-unix.authority: fs: stat candidate binaries on PATH directories (unix exec bit)
compose-probe-unix.reason: The unix is_executable only calls metadata on `<PATH dir>/<name>` for the binary names manifests mention and checks is_file plus an 0o111 mode bit, never opening or running the file.

compose-probe-other.authority: fs: stat candidate binaries on PATH directories (non-unix)
compose-probe-other.reason: On non-unix targets is_executable falls back to metadata().is_file() for the same manifest-named PATH candidates, keeping the binary probe read-only.

compose-apply-target.authority: fs: probe for ./aho.toml in the project directory
compose-apply-target.reason: apply_target only checks whether `<project>/aho.toml` is a file to choose the most specific layer, falling back to `~/.aho/config.toml` without touching either.

compose-list-loadouts.reason: list reads the loadouts directory under home and returns sorted `*.toml` stems, treating a missing directory as no loadouts.

session-index-rebuild.authority: fs: list the canonical sessions directory
session-index-rebuild.reason: rebuild enumerates `<sessions root>/*.jsonl`, accepting only stems that are the canonical hex spelling of a session id so duplicate aliases and path traversal cannot enter the index.

session-index-source.authority: fs: read one session JSONL source file
session-index-source.reason: load_session symlink_metadata-checks the path and refuses non-regular files (symlinks are not indexed) before streaming the session's JSONL lines into SQLite.

session-index-open.authority: fs: create/canonicalize the sessions directory and open the SQLite index
session-index-open.reason: SessionIndex::open creates and canonicalizes the sessions directory and opens the database in WAL mode, then binds the database to that one root and errors if it belongs to another.

session-index-writer.reason: open_log materializes an empty `<hex id>.jsonl` inside the index's bound root within an immediate transaction so a new session log gets the same refresh semantics as every other before a JsonlLog writer is returned.

session-index-sync.authority: fs: open and fsync one session JSONL file
session-index-sync.reason: sync_source reopens only `<root>/<hex id>.jsonl` of this IndexedLog and calls sync_all so the log is durable before the index row is updated.

jsonl-open.authority: fs: read an existing JSONL log or create its parent directory
jsonl-open.reason: JsonlLog::open replays every line of the given log file into the in-memory log, or creates the parent directory when the file does not exist yet.

jsonl-append.authority: fs: append a line to the JSONL log file
jsonl-append.reason: write_line opens only this log's own path in create+append mode and writes one serialized entry plus newline, so existing history is never rewritten.

session-spill.authority: fs: write oversized tool output into the session spill directory
session-spill.reason: spill writes text exceeding the inline budget to `<spill_dir>/<content hash>.txt` and, if that write fails, emits an error event and keeps the output inline instead of truncating.

embed-minilm-read.authority: fs: read the pinned MiniLM model and tokenizer files
embed-minilm-read.reason: load reads model.onnx and tokenizer.json from the configured artifact directory with a size cap of limit+1 bytes and re-verifies the exact buffers handed to the runtime against the pinned digests.

embed-minilm-verify.authority: fs: open and hash an on-disk MiniLM artifact
embed-minilm-verify.reason: verify_file checks an artifact's size against the pinned revision and streams it through SHA-256 (and git-blob SHA-1 for the tokenizer) with a bounded reader, only reading the file.

embed-minilm-provision.authority: net: HTTPS download of pinned MiniLM artifacts into an operator-chosen directory
embed-minilm-provision.reason: provision_minilm is an explicit operator step that uses an https_only client with timeouts, verifies rather than overwrites existing files, publishes atomically, touches no network when both artifacts already verify, and is never called by Embed::embed.

foreign-cli-workspace.authority: fs: canonicalize the sandbox policy workspace as the foreign CLI's cwd
foreign-cli-workspace.reason: spawn_inner canonicalizes policy.workspace() so the tmux-launched foreign CLI starts in the resolved sandbox workspace and that absolute cwd is what gets recorded in the subagent's state.

foreign-cli-binary-discovery.authority: env: PATH lookup of a foreign CLI binary
foreign-cli-binary-discovery.reason: which resolves a configured binary name the way a shell does, taking a value containing `/` as a path and otherwise checking is_file on each PATH entry, without executing anything.

foreign-cli-transcript-identity.authority: fs: stat a foreign CLI transcript file
foreign-cli-transcript-identity.reason: file_ident only calls metadata on the transcript path to derive its file identity (None when missing or not on unix), which lets the tailer detect replacement.

foreign-cli-transcript-read.authority: fs: incremental read of a foreign CLI transcript file
foreign-cli-transcript-read.reason: poll opens the transcript, treats a missing file as `exists: false` because the CLI writes lazily, and reads only complete lines appended since the last offset with a bounded take.

foreign-cli-tmux.authority: process: tmux client commands on aho's dedicated tmux socket
foreign-cli-tmux.reason: run spawns the configured tmux binary always with aho's own socket flag, strips AHO_READY_FD, sets kill_on_drop and bounds each call with COMMAND_TIMEOUT.

gc-process-probe.reason: probe runs ps for a single recorded pid only to read its state and elapsed time, so gc can decide whether an artifact's owner process is still alive before reclaiming it.

gc-process-signal.authority: process: `kill -s <sig>` to a recorded child's process group
gc-process-signal.reason: signal sends a signal to the process group of a pid gc already identified as its orphaned child, falling back to the lone pid when it leads no group, and reports kill's stderr on failure.

gc-git-command.authority: process: git command builder with repository env vars removed
gc-git-command.reason: command builds a `git` invocation after stripping GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE and the other REPO_ENV variables, so gc's git calls target only the explicit --git-dir it passes.

gc-git-run.authority: process: run a git command to completion for gc
gc-git-run.reason: run executes a command from git::command and maps a non-zero exit to an error carrying git's own stderr, so gc never acts on a failed git read.

gc-artifact-age.authority: fs: symlink_metadata mtime of a gc candidate
gc-artifact-age.reason: age_of reads only the modification time of a candidate path via symlink_metadata (symlinks are not followed), returning None when unreadable, to enforce gc's grace period.

gc-reclaim-spill.authority: fs: remove reclaimed spill files and worktrees listed in a gc report
gc-reclaim-spill.reason: reclaim deletes only items that the report lists and that a fresh scan still lists as reclaimable, and a failed removal is reported as still present.

gc-session-directory.authority: fs: list the session log directory
gc-session-directory.reason: read_all collects every `*.jsonl` below the session directory, treating a missing directory as holding no sessions and an unlistable one as an error.

gc-session-walk.authority: fs: recursive directory walk for session logs
gc-session-walk.reason: walk recurses through subdirectories of the session dir and collects only regular files with a `.jsonl` extension.

gc-snapshot-index.authority: process: git cat-file/ls-files over a shadow snapshot repository
gc-snapshot-index.reason: Repo::load runs `git --git-dir <shadow> cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch-check` and, when an index exists, `ls-files --stage` to build gc's view of a shadow repository's objects without modifying it.

gc-snapshot-object-size.authority: fs: stat loose objects of a shadow repository
gc-snapshot-object-size.reason: loose_files calls metadata on the loose-object files of the given ids to learn their on-disk sizes, leaving packed objects alone as not gc's to cut.

gc-snapshot-read-trees.authority: process: `git cat-file --batch` fed tree ids over stdin
gc-snapshot-read-trees.reason: read_trees spawns one git::command cat-file --batch on a shadow repository, writes tree ids to its stdin from a thread and parses the output strictly as tree listings.

gc-snapshot-repositories.authority: fs: canonicalize the project and list worktrees to locate shadow repositories
gc-snapshot-repositories.reason: repos canonicalizes the project and its `.aho/worktrees` entries and checks `<shadow dir>/<id prefix>.git` directories, finding only this project's shadow repositories.

gc-snapshot-delete.authority: fs: delete unreferenced loose objects from a shadow repository
gc-snapshot-delete.reason: delete removes loose objects reachable only from roots it rechecks as unreferenced and older than the grace period, and on error reports bytes already freed while leaving remaining objects intact.

gc-spill-scan.authority: fs: list `*.spill` directories and their `.txt` files under the session dir
gc-spill-scan.reason: judge reads the session directory for `*.spill` dirs and stats their regular `.txt` files to report size and ownership, performing no deletion itself.

gc-state-load.authority: fs: read the gc state file
gc-state-load.reason: load reads the previous scan's list of missing owners from the gc state file, and no file means no previous scan.

gc-state-save.authority: fs: atomic write of the gc state file
gc-state-save.reason: save creates the state file's directory and replaces the file via write-to-temp plus rename so a crashed gc never leaves a partial state file.

gc-worktree-root.authority: fs: canonicalize a session log's workspace root
gc-worktree-root.reason: names_root canonicalizes the root a session log names and compares it with the project base to decide whether that log belongs to this project's worktree.

gc-worktree-size.authority: fs: recursive size walk of a worktree directory
gc-worktree-size.reason: size_of sums file sizes below a worktree using symlink_metadata so symlinks are not followed and unreadable entries are skipped.

gc-worktree-scan.authority: fs: canonicalize the project and list `.aho/worktrees` git checkouts
gc-worktree-scan.reason: judge enumerates entries of the project's worktree directory that contain `.git` and reports them as candidates with ownership and liveness, deleting nothing.

hooks-claude-code-config.authority: env: current working directory as default hooks project dir
hooks-claude-code-config.reason: from_loadout falls back to std::env::current_dir only when hooks.claude_code.project_dir is unset, and resolves the Claude Code settings files relative to that project.

hooks-claude-code-settings.authority: fs: read Claude Code settings files for hook definitions
hooks-claude-code-settings.reason: build reads each configured settings file to parse hook groups, and a missing or unparsable file is recorded in status instead of failing the build.

hooks-claude-code-command.authority: process: `sh -c` hook commands in the project directory
hooks-claude-code-command.reason: run_command runs a configured Claude Code hook through sh with current_dir set to the project, pipes the JSON payload on stdin, strips AHO_READY_FD, and kills the child on timeout.

llm-anthropic-egress.authority: net: HTTPS client for the Anthropic Messages API
llm-anthropic-egress.reason: http_client builds the reqwest client this provider uses, with CONNECT_TIMEOUT set, and is the provider's only place for constructing network egress.

llm-anthropic-send.authority: net: POST to the configured Anthropic-compatible messages endpoint
llm-anthropic-send.reason: run posts one model request to the configured base_url (or the Copilot endpoint for github-copilot) with the resolved credential and maps transport failures and retry-after into LlmError.

llm-completions-egress.authority: net: HTTPS client for OpenAI chat completions
llm-completions-egress.reason: http_client builds the connect-timeout-bounded reqwest client the chat-completions provider uses for every request.

llm-completions-send.reason: run sends one chat-completions request to the configured base URL (or the Copilot endpoint when authenticated for it) and streams the response into the sink.

llm-responses-egress.authority: net: HTTPS client for the OpenAI Responses API
llm-responses-egress.reason: http_client builds the reqwest client with a 30 s connect timeout that the Responses transport reuses for every request.

llm-responses-send.authority: net: POST streaming request to the configured Responses endpoint
llm-responses-send.reason: run posts one request to endpoint(base, flavor) with `accept: text/event-stream` and maps transport errors and headers into the provider's LlmError.

llm-pi-messages-egress.authority: net: HTTPS client for the pi messages API
llm-pi-messages-egress.reason: http_client builds the reqwest client with a 30 s connect timeout used by this provider's messages transport.

llm-pi-messages-send.reason: run sends one messages request to the configured base URL and converts retry-after and transport failures into LlmError.

memory-local-config.authority: env: HOME and current directory as memory store defaults
memory-local-config.reason: build uses $HOME and the current directory only when memory.home / memory.project are not configured, and fails with a message naming `aho set memory.home` when HOME is unset.

memory-local-store-open.authority: fs: read a local memory store file
memory-local-store-open.reason: Store::open reads the scope's store file and reports a permissions error that names `memory.home`, so the memory provider reads only its own store path.

memory-local-store-flush.authority: fs: atomic write of a local memory store file
memory-local-store-flush.reason: flush writes the store only when something changed since the last save, creating its directory and replacing the file via temp write plus rename.

net-userspace-dns.authority: net: host-side DNS resolution for guest queries
net-userspace-dns.reason: The dns module backs runtime.rs's dns::resolve(query, nic, nics, config, policy) and dns::refused, which answer a guest's DNS query on a dedicated aho-net-dns thread under the network policy, with at most 32 lookups pending.

net-userspace-store.authority: fs: private network state directory, lock file and network.json
net-userspace-store.reason: Store creates the network directory with mode 0700, refuses symlinked lock or state files, takes a 0600 lock file, reads network.json capped at 4 MiB, and saves it by create_new temp file, rename and directory fsync.

net-userspace-runtime.authority: net: host TCP/UDP sockets for guest NAT flows and port maps
net-userspace-runtime.reason: The runtime terminates guest TCP in smoltcp and opens host TcpStream/UdpSocket connections only for flows the policy allows, binding host listeners only for configured PortMap entries, so no host interface is exposed to a guest.

auth-callback-listener.authority: net: loopback TCP listener for the OAuth redirect callback
auth-callback-listener.reason: bind listens only on 127.0.0.1 at the requested port for the browser's OAuth redirect and derives redirect_uri from the bound address, failing with CallbackUnavailable otherwise.

auth-http-client.authority: net: shared HTTPS client for provider login flows
auth-http-client.reason: Engine::new builds one process-wide reqwest client with a 10 s connect timeout and redirects disabled, so login token exchanges cannot be redirected elsewhere.

auth-http-send.authority: net: send a login-flow HTTP request
auth-http-send.reason: send executes a RequestBuilder built on the engine's client and maps failures to AuthError, providing the single egress point for provider login flows.

auth-kimi-host-env.reason: kimi_host reads only the two Kimi OAuth host variables, ignoring empty values, and otherwise defaults to https://auth.kimi.com.

auth-store-persist.authority: fs: atomic replace of the credential store file
auth-store-persist.reason: persist writes the document to a create_new `.auth-<random>.pending` file in the store's directory, renames it over the store and fsyncs the directory so credentials are never partially written.

auth-store-open.authority: fs: open the credential store with private-permission checks
auth-store-open.reason: private_open opens the store file (creating it only when asked) and runs check_private on its metadata so a store readable by others is refused.

auth-store-directory.authority: fs: create and lock down the credential store directory to 0700
auth-store-directory.reason: secure_directory creates the directory with mode 0700, refuses it unless it is a real directory owned by the effective uid, and tightens group/other bits through an O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY handle.

pty-host-working-directory.authority: process: spawn a PTY program in a directory under the host root
pty-host-working-directory.reason: start resolves the terminal's cwd against the host root (relative paths join the root), refuses a non-directory, spawns the program on a PTY slave and kills the tree if the reader threads fail.

pty-host-procfs.authority: fs: read /proc/<pid>/stat for the process tree (Linux)
pty-host-procfs.reason: list_proc reads /proc and each process's stat file only to extract ppid, pgid and sid so the PTY host can find the processes of a terminal's session.

pty-host-ps.authority: process: `ps` listing for the process tree (non-Linux)
pty-host-ps.reason: list_ps runs /bin/ps (or ps from PATH) to list processes and parses the output with getsid, as the non-Linux replacement for reading /proc.

selfdev-remove-channel.authority: fs: remove a channel symlink if present
selfdev-remove-channel.reason: remove_if_present deletes a channel link path and treats NotFound as success, so clearing a channel or its staging link is idempotent.

selfdev-publish.authority: fs: copy a build into read-only `versions/<hash>/aho`
selfdev-publish.reason: publish reads the binary, stages it in a temp dir under versions, sets it read-only and renames it into `versions/<hash>`, re-hashing when another publisher of the same bytes won the rename.

selfdev-verify-build.authority: fs: re-read a published build for hash verification
selfdev-verify-build.reason: verify re-reads `versions/<hash>/aho` and checks its bytes against the hash so a channel is never pointed at a tampered or truncated build.

selfdev-read-channel.authority: fs: read_link of a selfdev channel symlink
selfdev-read-channel.reason: channel reads the symlink of a named channel under the builds root and returns the build hash it points at, or None when the link is absent.

selfdev-point-channel.authority: fs: atomically repoint a channel symlink at `versions/<hash>`
selfdev-point-channel.reason: point creates a `.<name>.tmp` symlink to `versions/<hash>` and renames it over the channel link, or removes the link when no hash is given.

selfdev-activate.authority: fs: flip selfdev channels to a verified published build
selfdev-activate.reason: activate refuses a non-hash or unpublished build, then points each requested channel at it with an atomic symlink rename and restores earlier channels if a later flip fails.

selfdev-smoke.authority: process: smoke-boot a candidate build in a throwaway HOME/project tempdir
selfdev-smoke.reason: run_smoke creates a tempdir with fresh project and home dirs, runs the candidate binary's `plan --json` there with HOME overridden and AHO_READY_FD removed, and kills its process group on timeout.

selfdev-kill-smoke.authority: process: `kill` the smoke binary's process group
selfdev-kill-smoke.reason: kill_group signals the process group of the smoke-boot child (its grandchildren share it via process_group(0)) with AHO_READY_FD removed, so a hung smoke boot leaves nothing running.

selfdev-home.reason: build reads HOME only to expand a `~`-prefixed selfdev.builds_dir into the builds root the selfdev capability manages.

skills-fsdir-scan.authority: fs: read skill directories and SKILL.md / *.md files
skills-fsdir-scan.reason: scan lists each configured skill root, skips missing roots, refuses skill files over MAX_SKILL_BYTES and parses file text as Untrusted, turning unreadable entries into Broken rows.

skills-fsdir-resources.authority: fs: bounded listing of a skill directory's resource files
skills-fsdir-resources.reason: resources walks a skill directory and returns relative, sorted, bounded paths of its files, excluding SKILL.md and hidden entries.

skills-fsdir-config.authority: env: current directory and HOME as default skill roots
skills-fsdir-config.reason: from_loadout uses the current directory and $HOME only when skills.project_dir / skills.home_dir are unset, to locate the default project and user skill roots.

subagent-acp-program.authority: env: PATH lookup of an ACP agent program
subagent-acp-program.reason: resolve_program takes a program containing a separator as-is and otherwise returns the first PATH entry where the file exists, without running it.

subagent-acp-launch.authority: process: spawn a configured ACP agent command in the subagent cwd
subagent-acp-launch.reason: launch starts the agent command from caps.subagent-acp.agents.<name>.command in the given cwd with AHO_READY_FD removed and kill_on_drop set, or connects through a configured connector instead.

subagent-claude-locate.authority: fs: find a Claude Code transcript under the config dir's projects
subagent-claude-locate.reason: locate checks the direct transcript path for the session, then searches `<config_dir>/projects/*/<session>` for a regular file, only reading directory listings.

subagent-claude-config.authority: env: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and HOME for the Claude config directory
subagent-claude-config.reason: from_loadout inherits CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or falls back to `$HOME/.claude`, only when the loadout does not configure the directory, so transcripts are located where Claude Code writes them.

subagent-codex-transcript-directories.authority: fs: list numeric year/month/day directories of Codex sessions
subagent-codex-transcript-directories.reason: numeric_dirs lists a Codex sessions directory, keeps only all-digit subdirectory names and returns the newest `keep` of them to bound the transcript search.

subagent-codex-session-meta.authority: fs: read the first line of a Codex rollout file
subagent-codex-session-meta.reason: session_meta reads only the first line of a rollout and returns its payload when it is a session_meta record.

subagent-codex-transcript-modified.authority: fs: mtime of a Codex rollout file
subagent-codex-transcript-modified.reason: modified_ms reads only a rollout's modification time, used to rank candidate transcripts.

subagent-codex-workspace.authority: fs: canonicalize a rollout's recorded cwd
subagent-codex-workspace.reason: same_dir canonicalizes the cwd recorded in a Codex session_meta to compare it with the subagent's workspace when the strings differ.

subagent-codex-locate.authority: fs: scan recent Codex day directories for this subagent's rollout
subagent-codex-locate.reason: locate reads recent day directories and accepts only a rollout whose session_meta cwd matches the subagent cwd and that is its own thread rather than a fork or child.

subagent-codex-config.authority: env: CODEX_HOME and HOME for the Codex home directory
subagent-codex-config.reason: from_loadout inherits CODEX_HOME, or falls back to `$HOME/.codex`, only when subagent.codex.home is not configured.

vm-guest-connect.authority: net: unix-socket connection to the in-guest agent
vm-guest-connect.reason: connect opens the configured guest-agent socket path and runs a reader thread that routes responses to pending request ids, erroring with setup guidance when the socket is absent.

vm-guest-agent-endpoint.authority: fs: open the virtio agent port or bind a fixture unix socket (guest side)
vm-guest-agent-endpoint.reason: run parses `--workspace` plus exactly one of `--device` (opened read/write) or `--socket` (bound as a UnixListener fixture) and serves the host's agent protocol on it.

vm-rfb-connect.authority: net: unix-socket connection to a VM's RFB display
vm-rfb-connect.reason: connect opens the manager-selected display socket with read and write timeouts and wraps it with the caller's guard, normally a VM lease check.

world-host-egress-client.authority: net: HTTP client for host-world egress
world-host-egress-client.reason: HostEgress::new builds a reqwest client with automatic redirects disabled and a connect timeout, so every redirect hop is returned to the egress layer to re-check.

world-host-egress-exchange.authority: net: perform one policy-approved egress HTTP exchange from the host
world-host-egress-exchange.reason: exchange sends the approved request, surfaces Location for manual redirect handling and reads the body chunk by chunk so it can stop at the size limit.

world-host-fs.authority: fs: host-disk Fs seam fenced to the workspace root
world-host-fs.reason: The fs module canonicalizes the workspace root once, refuses `..` escapes and symlinks leaving or dangling from the root, and makes every write atomic via temp file plus rename in the same directory.

world-host-config.authority: env: current directory, HOME and SHELL as host-world defaults
world-host-config.reason: from_loadout uses the current directory for workspace.root, `$HOME/.aho/shadow` for the shadow dir and $SHELL (else /bin/sh) only when the loadout leaves those keys unset.

world-host-worktree-git.authority: process: git subcommands under the project worktree
world-host-worktree-git.reason: git_in runs git in the given directory with GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE removed, so worktree setup acts on that repository only.

world-host-worktree-root.authority: fs: create/canonicalize `.aho/worktrees/<name>` via git worktree add
world-host-worktree-root.reason: ensure_worktree reuses an existing `.aho/worktrees/<name>` checkout or runs `git worktree add` on branch aho/<name> after verifying a repository exists, then returns the canonical path.

world-host-build-root.authority: fs: canonicalize the configured workspace root
world-host-build-root.reason: build canonicalizes cfg.root so the host world's fs and shell seams are fenced to one resolved workspace directory.

world-host-snapshot-git.authority: process: git against the shadow checkpoint store
world-host-snapshot-git.reason: git runs git with `--git-dir=<shadow store>` and current_dir at the workspace root, feeding optional stdin and turning a failed command into an FsError naming the shadow store.

world-host-snapshot-store.authority: fs: create and init the shadow checkpoint git store
world-host-snapshot-store.reason: ensure is a no-op once HEAD exists, and otherwise creates the parent directory, runs SHA-256 `git init` under clean_env, and writes an info/exclude that ignores `.aho/`.

world-host-snapshot-restore.authority: fs: restore workspace files from a checkpoint tree
world-host-snapshot-restore.reason: restore verifies the target is a tree, then uses read-tree and checkout-index in the shadow store and deletes only non-directory paths the checkpoint does not contain.

world-host-snapshot-prune.authority: fs: remove empty parent directories inside the workspace root
world-host-snapshot-prune.reason: prune_empty_parents walks up from a deleted file, calling remove_dir only on directories strictly inside the root, and stops at the first non-empty one.

world-ssh-egress-hop.authority: process: ssh-run curl on the remote host for egress
world-ssh-egress-hop.reason: hop runs one curl over the world's ssh command with kill_on_drop, stops reading at headers plus max_body+1 bytes and kills the transfer there, and maps exit codes to specific egress errors.

world-ssh-config-home.authority: env: HOME expansion of `~/` in ssh world paths
world-ssh-config-home.reason: expand_home replaces a leading `~/` with $HOME for configured ssh paths (identity, config, known_hosts, control dir) and leaves other paths unchanged.

world-ssh-config-cwd.authority: env: current directory to anchor a relative ssh control_dir
world-ssh-config-cwd.reason: from_loadout joins a relative world.ssh.control_dir or session-dir default onto std::env::current_dir, so the control socket location does not change with later cwd changes.

world-ssh-command.authority: process: tokio ssh client command to the configured target
world-ssh-command.reason: command builds `ssh <options> -- <host> <remote>` from the world's Target options with stdio unset, so every async remote call goes through one option set.

world-ssh-std-command.authority: process: blocking ssh client command to the configured target
world-ssh-std-command.reason: std_command is the std::process twin of command, with the same options and `--` host separator, for synchronous callers.

world-ssh-run.authority: process: run a script on the remote host over ssh
world-ssh-run.reason: run spawns the ssh command with kill_on_drop, feeds input (or /dev/null) to stdin, and reports only ssh-level failures as Err while a script's non-zero exit is returned in Out.

world-ssh-run-blocking.authority: process: blocking remote script over ssh for Capability::build
world-ssh-run-blocking.reason: run_blocking runs the script through std_command with stdin null, used only where Capability::build is synchronous.

world-ssh-close-master.authority: process: `ssh -O exit` to stop the control master on drop
world-ssh-close-master.reason: Drop runs ssh to stop the control master so no connection outlives the world, treating no running master as the normal case.

world-ssh-effective-config.authority: process: `ssh -G` to resolve effective host settings
world-ssh-effective-config.reason: effective runs `ssh -G` for the target only to read the effective hostname, port, user and known_hosts, and connects to nothing.

world-ssh-control-directory.authority: fs: create the private (0700) ssh control directory
world-ssh-control-directory.reason: create_private_dir creates the control-socket directory recursively with mode 0700 and reports a failure naming world.ssh.control_dir.

vm-image-create.authority: process: qemu-img create for a VM-owned disk
vm-image-create.reason: create_disk runs the configured qemu_img to create one owned disk at the machine's disk path and size, optionally backed by a base, and keeps the disk for inspection on failure.

vm-supervisor-spawn.authority: process: spawn the aho-vm-supervisor for a machine
vm-supervisor-spawn.reason: start_any launches the configured supervisor in its own process group and kills it unless QEMU exposes an owned QMP socket in the machine directory within 15 seconds.

vm-destroy.authority: fs: remove a VM's machine directory
vm-destroy.reason: destroy is operator cleanup that drops the machine's network proxy and removes its machine directory, which is permitted after lease revocation when lab effects are not.

vm-console-write.authority: net: unix-socket write to a VM's console socket
vm-console-write.reason: console_write connects to `<machine dir>/console.sock` of the named VM and writes the given bytes to the guest console, and is unix-only.

vm-media-import.authority: fs: copy an operator-supplied file into immutable 0400 VM media storage
vm-media-import.reason: import_media refuses existing names and empty or non-regular sources, has qemu-img reject qcow2 files with backing or data files, then copies with create_new and marks the copy 0400.

vm-network-listen.authority: net: unix-socket listener that attaches a VM NIC to the userspace network
vm-network-listen.reason: listen replaces a stale socket file, binds the per-VM network socket and relays each accepted stream to an attachment of the configured Network.

vm-qmp-connect.authority: net: unix-socket QMP command to QEMU
vm-qmp-connect.reason: command connects to a machine's QMP socket, requires QEMU's greeting, negotiates qmp_capabilities and executes exactly one command.

vm-state-directory.authority: fs: create a 0700 VM state directory
vm-state-directory.reason: directory creates the VM state path, sets mode 0700 on unix and returns its canonical form for all later VM storage.

vm-state-read.authority: fs: read a VM state JSON file
vm-state-read.reason: load opens a VM state file and refuses anything over 8 MiB before deserializing.

vm-state-save.authority: fs: atomic write of a VM state JSON file
vm-state-save.reason: save writes to a create_new `.write-<uuid>` sibling, renames it over the target and fsyncs the parent directory.

vm-state-lock.authority: fs: open a VM lock file
vm-state-lock.reason: lock opens the machine lock file read/write, creating it without truncation, to hold an exclusive lock on the VM state.

vm-state-list.authority: fs: list a VM storage directory
vm-state-list.reason: entries lists the paths in a VM storage directory, sorted, so records are enumerated deterministically.

vm-media-hash.authority: fs: read a media file to hash it
vm-media-hash.reason: hash streams a media file to compute the content hash recorded for immutable VM media.

vm-supervisor-output.authority: fs: persist QEMU stdout/stderr scrollback in the machine directory
vm-supervisor-output.reason: capture runs a thread that reads a QEMU output pipe into a capacity-bounded ring persisted to console.json or stderr.json in the machine directory, resuming an existing file.

vm-supervisor-console.authority: net: unix-socket console listener feeding QEMU stdin
vm-supervisor-console.reason: console replaces a stale socket, binds the machine's console socket and forwards accepted connections to the QEMU child's stdin until stopped.

vm-supervisor-launch.authority: process: run QEMU under the aho-vm-supervisor binary
vm-supervisor-launch.reason: supervise is the installed supervisor's entry point, launching the recorded QEMU binary and args from the launch file only under the lease budget and killing QEMU when the lease ends; it never executes guest commands.

rpc-unix-listener.authority: net: 0600 unix-socket listener for the rpc surface
rpc-unix-listener.reason: serve_unix refuses to replace a socket another server still answers on, removes a stale file, binds, chmods the socket 0600 and serves each connection against the session.

web-listener.authority: net: TCP listener for the web UI
web-listener.reason: The web surface binds its configured address only after refusing plain HTTP on a non-loopback address, so non-loopback serving always has TLS.

webhook-tls-input.authority: fs: read the webhook TLS certificate/key PEM files
webhook-tls-input.reason: read_pem reads the configured surface.webhook cert or key file and names which one could not be read.

webhook-listener.authority: net: TCP listener for the GitHub webhook surface
webhook-listener.reason: The webhook surface binds only once a transport is configured and refuses plain HTTP off loopback, so any exposed webhook listener uses TLS.

auth-browser-opener.authority: process: platform URL opener (open / rundll32 / xdg-open) for login
auth-browser-opener.reason: open launches the platform's URL opener with only the login URL, null stdio and AHO_READY_FD removed, and reaps it on a thread.

cli-config.authority: fs: read patch files and write lock files for config verbs
cli-config.reason: The config module reads operator-named patch files and writes the lock file into the most specific layer after the plan → diff → `apply? [y/N]` flow.

cli-ctx.authority: env: current directory, NO_COLOR and project paths for every CLI verb
cli-ctx.reason: ctx is the shared CLI plumbing that resolves the project by canonicalizing the launch directory, lists session files, checks NO_COLOR for terminal output and uses ps to test recorded pids.

cli-history.authority: process: git and tar for fork/diff/merge/destroy of worktree sessions
cli-history.reason: history runs git (under clean_git) and tar against a session's canonical workspace and shadow store, extracting trees into a tempfile scratch dir to fork, diff, merge or remove worktrees.

cli-invariants.authority: process: java/TLC for formal invariant checks, with tempdir scratch under .aho
cli-invariants.reason: invariants probes the configured java, writes counterexamples and spill reads under the session dir, and generates TLA specs in a tempdir inside the project's `.aho` directory for `aho invariants` and `session verify --formal`.

cli-ops.authority: process: operator-confirmed curl/sh installers plus doctor/apply file IO
cli-ops.reason: ops reads apply inputs, keeps doctor logs under `~/.aho/doctor`, looks up tools on PATH, and runs curl or the Lean installer only after the operator confirms the printed plan.

cli-rpc-bridge.authority: net: 0600 unix-socket bridge to the serving daemon
cli-rpc-bridge.reason: rpc_bridge speaks the rpc protocol on stdio or on a `--socket` it binds 0600 after refusing to replace a live server, and forwards frames to the daemon's socket.

cli-selfdev.authority: fs: create the selfdev builds directory and connect to the daemon
cli-selfdev.reason: selfdev_cmd creates the builds root and connects to the running daemon's socket to publish, smoke, flip channels and hand over during `aho selfdev reload`.

cli-serve.authority: process: re-exec the aho binary as a detached daemon with a project log
cli-serve.reason: serve spawns the running aho executable (current_exe) with the operator's --set/--disable flags, appending output to `<project>/.aho/daemon.log`, and connects thin clients to its unix socket.

cli-session.authority: process: operator shell or program in the session workspace
cli-session.reason: session runs the verbs that open a session log, including `aho shell`, which starts $SHELL (else /bin/sh) or a given program in the session workspace, and removes session files it owns.

cli-spec.reason: spec reads spec/SPEC.md for `status`/`render` and writes the rendered file back when asked.

cli-surfaces.authority: process: openssl for `aho cert` plus TLS file IO for long-lived surfaces
cli-surfaces.reason: surfaces reads TLS files for the web and webhook surfaces and implements `aho cert`, running openssl into a directory and installing the key 0600 via rename.

daemon-crash-probe.reason: Crash detection compares a recorded (pid, start_time) with the live process table; the daemon itself always runs on the host (07), so this probe is host lifecycle, not a tool effect.

daemon-ready-env.reason: The exec-in-place reload handshake (12) passes the readiness descriptor through the environment; it is read once at startup before anything can spawn and inherit it.

daemon-ready-spawn.authority: process: spawn the detached daemon binary
daemon-ready-spawn.reason: `aho serve --detach` starts the daemon process and waits on its readiness pipe; daemon lifecycle is host-side by definition (07: the daemon always lives on the host).

daemon-ready-exec.authority: process: execve of the new daemon image in place
daemon-ready-exec.reason: Self-dev reload (12) replaces the daemon image with the same pid; only the daemon may do this, and only after quiescing sessions and stopping drivers.

daemon-serve-lifecycle.authority: fs: the sessions directory and the daemon's own socket file
daemon-serve-lifecycle.reason: Startup creates the project's session directory and shutdown removes the socket it bound; both are daemon-owned host paths, never workspace content.

daemon-fresh-id.reason: A new session id must not collide with a log already on disk; this is an existence probe on daemon-owned storage.

daemon-open-session.reason: Opening decides between creating and resuming a log (and whether a >64-bit id names an existing CLI log); the log itself is opened through SessionIndex.

daemon-socket-bind.authority: net+fs: bind the operator unix socket (0600) and clear a stale one
daemon-socket-bind.reason: The socket carries operator authority, so binding fails closed unless it can be restricted to this user; a stale socket nobody answers on is removed.

daemon-list-logs.reason: `session.list` and the crash scan enumerate daemon-owned logs; reads names only.

daemon-reload-binary.authority: fs: metadata of the reload binary
daemon-reload-binary.reason: Reload refuses before quiescing anything unless the named binary is an executable file.

daemon-client-connect.authority: net: connect to the daemon's operator unix socket
daemon-client-connect.reason: The CLI and bridges are clients of the local daemon (12); the socket is 0600, so connecting is operator authority, not agent egress.

daemon-reload-exec.authority: env+fs+process: current_exe, remove own socket, exec the new image
daemon-reload-exec.reason: daemon.reload persists recovery intents, quiesces, removes its own socket and execs the new binary in place; on failure it rebinds and keeps serving.

scripted-read-script.authority: fs: read the operator-named JSON script
scripted-read-script.reason: The deterministic model route loads `provider.scripted.script`, a file the operator names on the host; it is test/CI infrastructure and never reachable by the agent.

mcp-http-post.authority: net: HTTP POST to a configured MCP endpoint
mcp-http-post.reason: Streamable-HTTP MCP sends JSON-RPC requests to the endpoint the operator configured; the client was built by http_client with the egress list checked on every hop.

mcp-http-stream.authority: net: HTTP GET of the server's notification stream
mcp-http-stream.reason: The same configured MCP endpoint's SSE stream, under the handshake timeout; same egress-checked client.

mcp-http-session-close.authority: net: HTTP DELETE ending the MCP session
mcp-http-session-close.reason: Dropping the last handle tells the configured server the session ended, as the MCP HTTP transport requires.

mcp-http-client.authority: net: construct the reqwest client for MCP endpoints
mcp-http-client.reason: The single construction point for MCP HTTP traffic; its redirect policy checks each hop against egress.allow/egress.deny (07: under host, egress is enforced by tool.check on web tools and MCP).

world-host-transport.authority: process: spawn a host child with separate protocol pipes
world-host-transport.reason: The host world's Subprocess provider (07) is the process authority for world=host; this adds the lossless stdin/stdout/stderr transport MCP servers use, in the same process group model.

world-ssh-transport.authority: process: ssh over the world's control master with separate protocol pipes
world-ssh-transport.reason: The ssh world's Subprocess provider; the child runs on the remote host, with the transport pipes carried by the local ssh client.

world-ssh-kill-group.authority: process: ssh control command signalling the remote process group
world-ssh-kill-group.reason: Killing a remote child (TERM, grace, KILL) must reach its whole remote process group, which only a control command over the master can do.

world-ssh-drop-cleanup.authority: process: best-effort remote group kill for an abandoned child
world-ssh-drop-cleanup.reason: A child nobody holds any more cannot be waited on; its remote group is killed so it cannot outlive the session.

formal-extract-write.authority: fs: write/remove SPEC.md extracts under the operator's spec/ directory
formal-extract-write.reason: Only `aho spec render` (operator CLI) calls this; it writes marker-carrying extracts and never touches files without the marker. Agent tools materialize through FsWrite scratch instead.

formal-extract-scan.authority: fs: list and read spec/tla and spec/lean
formal-extract-scan.reason: Finds extract-marked files so render can remove stale extracts and status can report orphans; operator CLI only.

formal-extract-freshness.authority: fs: read SPEC.md extracts under spec/
formal-extract-freshness.reason: `aho spec status` compares on-disk extracts with what SPEC.md produces, byte for byte; operator CLI only.

sdk-client-spawn.authority: process: spawn `aho rpc` as the SDK's session server
sdk-client-spawn.reason: An embedder's SDK client drives aho through the rpc surface on stdio (08); starting that process is the embedder's own operator authority.

sdk-client-connect.authority: net: connect to an `aho rpc --socket` unix socket
sdk-client-connect.reason: The same rpc surface over a 0600 unix socket the embedder chose; operator transport, not agent egress.

sdk-codegen-dir.authority: fs: canonicalize this checkout's sdk/ directory
sdk-codegen-dir.reason: Build-time generator location for the TypeScript/Python SDKs (`aho-sdk` codegen), never used by a session.

sdk-codegen-write.authority: fs: write generated SDK files under sdk/
sdk-codegen-write.reason: Regenerates the thin SDKs from the protocol table, writing only files whose content changed.

sdk-codegen-drift.authority: fs: read generated SDK files under sdk/
sdk-codegen-drift.reason: The drift gate compares checked-in generated files with a fresh render; read-only.

sdk-builder-project.authority: env+fs: current_dir and canonical project/script paths
sdk-builder-project.reason: An embedder builds an SDK instance for a project directory (default: where it runs) the way `aho` resolves its own; the result is captured Inputs.

sdk-workspace-root.reason: The host world's workspace root handed to Session::boot, resolved once from the embedder's configuration.

sdk-session-open.authority: fs: session log existence and the session index
sdk-session-open.reason: Resuming refuses an id with no log on disk; logs are opened through SessionIndex so SDK sessions are searchable like CLI ones.

daemon-ready-probe.authority: process: exec in place for the readiness-handshake tests
daemon-ready-probe.reason: Test helper binary for exec-in-place reload (12); it exists to exercise take_ready_fd/exec_with_ready exactly as a real reload does.

net-userspace-control.authority: net+fs: the network's control unix socket inside its private (0700) state directory
net-userspace-control.reason: A running network answers status and configure requests from the operator's `aho net` on `<state_dir>/ctl`; the directory is owner-only, so the socket carries exactly the authority of the user who already owns the network's state, and a stale socket is removed only while the state lock is held.

cli-net.authority: fs: read a session network's persisted network.json
cli-net.reason: `aho net status` reads a stopped network's persisted configuration without starting it; changes go through the network's own locked store or its control socket, never raw writes.

world-ns-boundary.authority: fs+process+namespaces: the sandbox's private state directory, the aho-ns-helper keeper, mounts and setns inside the helper
world-ns-boundary.reason: The namespace world's audited Linux boundary: on the host it creates the session's 0700 sandbox directory (recipe and seed copies), starts and signals the keeper by pidfd, and bridges the NIC socket; inside the dedicated single-threaded helper it builds the user/mount/net namespaces, pivots root and drops every capability before any sandbox command runs. Agent-supplied paths are only ever resolved inside the sandbox.

cli-sandbox.authority: fs+process: operator export target on the host, the operator shell into the sandbox
cli-sandbox.reason: `aho export` writes a copy of sandbox files to an operator-named host path (create-new only, every target checked before the first write); `aho shell` runs the namespace helper on the operator's terminal; `aho sandbox destroy` removes the session's own sandbox directory after confirmation. Sandbox contents are read through the world's Fs, never as host paths.

vm-state-exists.authority: fs: presence of VM state under the private VM directory
vm-state-exists.reason: The VM manager and supervisor check whether machine records, leases, scrollback and QEMU sockets exist inside the 0700 VM state directory they own; agent input is never a path here (machine names are validated labels).

vm-host-destroy.authority: fs+process: quit an owned QEMU over QMP and remove its machine directory
vm-host-destroy.reason: Operator `aho sandbox destroy` and `aho gc` remove a machine the owning session no longer needs: QEMU is stopped only after its QMP UUID matches the persisted record, and only the machine's own directory under the private VM state is removed.

gc-sandbox-scan.authority: fs: list sandbox and network directories in session.dir and VM owner state
gc-sandbox-scan.reason: `aho gc` finds `<id>.ns` / `<id>.net` directories and VM machines whose owning session log is gone (or whose lease ended) by listing aho's own state; reclaiming goes through each world's destroy path, never a raw delete of foreign paths.
